key_insight: Combined computational and neural-network modelling identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports process-window selection for HDPE joints by predicting temperatures, axial forces and defect formation.
method: Developed a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model of heat transfer, material flow and weld defects.
Trained two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Combined predictions to map defective and defect-free welding conditions.
evidence_signal: Experimental validation supported CEL predictions; ANNs achieved R² values of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Predictive performance outside the tested process-parameter space is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
